reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the premise that nanoscale trenches reduce TBReff at a GaN/diamond interface via increased contact area, but it provides no evidence regarding refractory HEAs, high-temperature mechanical loads, or structural integrity, leaving the key premise of transferability completely unsupported.
premises: Nanoscale trenches at an interface can reduce effective thermal boundary resistance (TBReff) by increasing contact area.
The TBReff reduction mechanism is consistent with increased contact area facilitating phonon transmission.
Nanosecond transient thermoreflectance (ns-TTR) can measure the reduction in TBReff.
The approach is transferable from a GaN/diamond interface to a refractory HEA interlayer interface under high-temperature, mechanical load conditions.
